question: Balancing Uber's 20% Gross Bookings scale against Waymo's Jan 2028 break, Uber's >$10B AV pivot, Delivery Hero debt, EU/FTC headwinds, and Stage 4 tape, what is our exact decision?

epigraph.quote: A strong operating business can still be a rejected stock when capital allocation pivots into debt-funded M&A and hardware commitments while the chart breaks into Stage 4.
epigraph.author: Institutional Capital Allocation Playbook

web_blocks.html: An honest decision weighs both sides of the debate before setting rules. On the Bull side, Uber's core operating flywheel remains formidable. Monthly Active Platform Consumers reached 215 million (+14% YoY) and quarterly trips hit 4,061 million (+16% YoY) [31, 32]. Q3 2026 Gross Bookings surged 20% YoY to $59.82 billion, Adjusted EBITDA reached $2.96 billion (5.0% of GB), and Q4 guidance calls for $63.25B–$65.25B in bookings [32]. Trailing Free Cash Flow hit $10.42 billion, Uber One surpassed 50 million members, and high-margin Advertising exceeded a $2.5 billion run-rate [3, 19]. Bulls argue that Uber's global demand graph—backed by 15+ AV partners including Lucid/Nuro, Wayve, Baidu, and WeRide—will make Uber the indispensable hybrid demand aggregator once autonomous supply commoditizes [18, 41].

On the Bear side, our Pass 1 blind-spot audit uncovered five structural frictions that materially alter the 2027–2028 risk-reward [31, 40–45]. First, Waymo confirmed it is ending Austin/Atlanta exclusivity to launch its standalone Waymo One app in January 2028 (>500,000 weekly paid trips), directly challenging Uber's AV aggregator moat [40]. Second, Uber is no longer purely asset-light: management committed over $10 billion to AV commercialization (~$2.5B direct equity in Lucid/Nuro et al. + ~$7.5B future fleet procurement/deployment milestones for >120,000 AVs) [41]. Third, quarterly buybacks were slashed 75% (from $3,010M in Q1 to $754M in Q3) as cash shifted to Delivery Hero (66.56% tender; H2 2027 close; EC/KFTC/MENA antitrust scrutiny over the Uber-backed SSW carve-out loan) and ezCater ($2.3B), pushing long-term debt up 49% to $15,664 million [31, 43]. Fourth, DoorDash's completed £2.9B Deliveroo acquisition intensifies European/MENA delivery competition [42]. Fifth, regulatory cash drains are stacking up: ~$1.5B Q4 2026 UK HMRC VAT payment, December 2, 2026 EU Platform Work Directive transposition, Australia's 6–1 payroll tax ruling (>AUD $100M), and the FTC + 21-state Uber One ROSCA lawsuit plus October 2026 FTC algorithmic pricing inquiry [39, 44, 45]. Paired with a Stage 4 tape inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend, buying here fails both trend and risk-reward tests.

web_blocks.takeaway: Independent 12-month expected value is $67.20 (+5.9% vs. $63.47 CMP)—far too thin against -33.8% Bear (-39.8% combined stress) to justify fighting a Stage 4 downtrend.

web_blocks.takeaway: New-capital verdict is REJECTED (TIER_0). Stage 4 CAP_REJECTED breakdown, thin +5.9% EV, and cash-flow/capital-allocation friction block new buys.

web_blocks.title: Dual Verdict: New Capital REJECTED (TIER_0) & Open LEAPS EXIT_IMMEDIATELY
paragraphs: New-Capital Verdict — REJECTED (TIER_0; Reasons: TREND, CASH_FLOW): Under Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED) and +5.9% expected value, common equity is strictly REJECTED. The snapshot-derived $61.24–$63.10 band ($60.96 screen stop) is purely a historical technical support reference carrying 0.0% bids; commit zero new equity or options cash until a full Stage 1 base and Stage 2 reclaim >$73.50 form.

Current Holding Action — NOT_HELD (0 Common Shares) / LEAPS EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH): Equity accounts hold 0 common shares (holding_shares_to_sell: 0). On the 5 open Robinhood Dec 17, 2027 Call LEAPS (4x $110C, 1x $100C; $3,463.86 cost; $1,775.86 recorded book mark = 2.22% of NAV; 392 DTE Nov 20 / 389 DTE Nov 23), we override the scanner and mandate EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH): both strikes expire at $0.00 intrinsic at our $70.00 Base Case (and all 4x $110C expire at $0.00 even at $105.00 Bull). Rather than gambling on an uncertain oversold relief rally while cash sits at 9.13% vs. the 22.0% floor, close all 5 contracts cleanly via limit orders near mid on bounce liquidity (~$64.60) into USD cash; zero averaging down; hard breach <= $63.00.

web_blocks.html: What Changes Our Verdict: Re-open UBER equity only after shares build a multi-week Stage 1 base and reclaim $72.40–$73.50 on >=1.25x volume, US breadth exits Downtrend, Delivery Hero tracks <2.0x net leverage without punitive remedies, and 2027 AV unit economics prove accretive. For the 5 open Dec 2027 LEAPS, execute EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH) now.

Protecting and rebuilding our $7,290.91 cash reserve (9.13% of $79,861.16 NAV) is paramount inside a 10-distribution-day US market Downtrend requiring a 22.0% cash floor. We keep 100% of marginal dollars in CASH. Unheld defensive healthcare leader AbbVie (ABBV, Stage 2, $286.20 Nov 20 / $289.49 live, $340.00 Base target) and outside insurer Arch Capital (ACGL, Stage 2, $108.82 Nov 20 / $109.05 live, $130.00 Base target) stay at 0% until portfolio cash approaches the Downtrend floor.

book_paragraphs: We have reached our final independent judgment, where Pass 1's five uncovered structural blind spots, Pass 2's AV- and SBC-adjusted valuation, and the Stage 4 price tape converge into one clear action plan. Let us weigh both sides of the aisle with total candor before locking in our rules.

On the Bull side, Uber's operating engine is genuinely world-class. Monthly Active Platform Consumers reached 215 million (+14% YoY), quarterly trips hit 4,061 million (+16% YoY), Q3 2026 Gross Bookings rose 20% to $59.82 billion, Adjusted EBITDA hit $2.96 billion (5.0% of bookings), and Q4 guidance points to $63.25 billion to $65.25 billion. Over 50 million Uber One members and a $2.5 billion-plus Advertising run-rate generate high-margin monetization. If autonomous vehicle supply ultimately commoditizes across 15-plus partners and plugs into Uber's demand graph to fill off-peak hours, Uber can compound earnings for a decade.

On the Bear side, however, five hard realities discovered in our audit fundamentally reshape the 2027–2028 risk profile. First, Waymo confirmed it is ending Uber exclusivity in Austin and Atlanta to launch its standalone Waymo One app in January 2028 after surpassing 500,000 weekly paid trips, directly refuting the assumption that AV leaders need Uber as an exclusive gateway. Second, Uber is no longer purely asset-light: management has committed over $10 billion toward AV commercialization (~$2.5 billion in direct equity stakes in Lucid, Nuro, and peers plus ~$7.5 billion in future fleet procurement and deployment milestones covering over 120,000 AVs). Third, quarterly buybacks fell 75% from $3.01 billion in Q1 to $754 million in Q3 as cash pivoted to Delivery Hero (66.56% tender, H2 2027 close, facing EC, KFTC, and MENA antitrust scrutiny over Uber's loan backing the SSW Partners carve-out) and ezCater ($2.3 billion), pushing long-term debt up 49% to $15.66 billion. Fourth, DoorDash's completed £2.9 billion Deliveroo acquisition intensifies international delivery competition. Fifth, regulatory cash drains are converging simultaneously: CFO Krishnamurthy's ~$1.5 billion Q4 2026 UK HMRC VAT payment, the December 2, 2026 EU Platform Work Directive transposition deadline, Australia's 6–1 payroll tax ruling exceeding AUD $100 million, and the FTC plus 21-state Uber One ROSCA lawsuit alongside the October 2026 FTC algorithmic pricing inquiry.

Pricing those realities into our independent AV- and SBC-adjusted DCF yields a $42.00 Bear target (35% weight, -33.8%; $38.19 under combined insurance-gap stress), a $70.00 Base target (45% weight, +10.3%), and a $105.00 Bull target (20% weight, +65.4%), weighting to a $67.20 12-month expected value—just +5.9% upside against -33.8% to -39.8% downside. Paired with a confirmed Stage 4 breakdown at $63.47 inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend (35.8% breadth above 50DMA), our New-Capital Verdict is strictly REJECTED (TIER_0; reasons: TREND and CASH_FLOW). We assign 0.0% equity bids, treat the $61.24–$63.10 pocket ($60.96 stop) strictly as a historical reference, and demand a full Stage 1 base plus Stage 2 reclaim above $73.50 before re-underwriting.

Across our three investment horizons, the rules are unambiguous. Over 1 to 12 weeks, Reject and Stay Away while Stage 4 supply controls every bounce. Over 3 to 12 months, REJECTED (TIER_0) keeps fresh dollars out of a falling knife while Q4 UK VAT outflows, EU Directive transposition, and Delivery Hero antitrust reviews play out. Over 2 to 5 years, Uber retains its COMPOUNDER_PASS quality rating with PASS_WITH_WATCH—earned by its global demand scale, but strictly conditional on proving Delivery Hero de-leveraging below 2.0x, positive ROIC on its >$10 billion AV commitments, and Mobility take-rate stability above 23%.

Our capital-redeployment rule is equally clear. Consolidated US cash stands at $7,290.91 ($4,772.99 Schwab plus $2,517.92 Robinhood), or 9.13% of our $79,861.16 consolidated US net worth—still well below the 22.0% cash floor prescribed during a 10-distribution-day Downtrend. We therefore retain 100% of marginal dollars in CASH, keeping unheld Stage 2 leaders AbbVie ($286.20, $340.00 Base) and Arch Capital Group ($108.82, $130.00 Base) at 0% until portfolio liquidity recovers.

Finally, our existing-position action is crystal clear. Equity accounts hold zero common Uber shares (NOT_HELD, sell 0 shares). On the 5 open December 17, 2027 Call LEAPS in Robinhood (4x $110C and 1x $100C; $3,463.86 cost; $1,775.86 recorded mark; 392 DTE as of November 20 / 389 DTE November 23), we override the mechanical scanner and mandate EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH). Because both strikes expire at $0.00 intrinsic value at our $70.00 Base Case—and all four $110 calls STILL expire worthless even in our $105.00 Bull Case—use relief-bounce liquidity (~$64.60) and limit orders near mid to salvage remaining time value into USD cash cleanly, with zero averaging down and hard invalidation at or below $63.00.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: DISCIPLINE BEATS ATTACHMENT
book_callouts.text: You can admire Uber's 215-million-user marketplace and still reject the stock at $63.47. When independent forensics cut expected value to +5.9%, expose >$10B in AV commitments and Waymo's Jan 2028 break, and confirm Stage 4 selling, capital preservation means 0% new equity and an immediate, orderly exit from all 5 out-of-the-money Dec 2027 LEAPS into cash.
